articles.title: Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry faced $10 million legal battle after branding company alleged breach of contract
articles.summary: Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry’s growing business profile came under legal scrutiny in 2020 when celebrity branding company Flutie Entertainment sued
articles.body: Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry’s growing business profile came under legal scrutiny in 2020 when celebrity branding company Flutie Entertainment sued her for more than $10 million. The lawsuit accused Curry of breaching a business agreement after she ended the company’s five-year relationship with her. The case also named six Curry-affiliated companies and a former Flutie employee who later worked directly with Curry.Ayesha Curry's business ventures became the focus of the lawsuitFlutie Entertainment filed the lawsuit in Los Angeles Superior Court in April 2020, claiming its work with Curry had helped build her profile as a food and lifestyle personality.According to the lawsuit, the company helped Ayesha secure a Food Network show and a hosting role on ABC’s “Great American Baking Show.” It also pointed to her bestselling cookbook and several food-related businesses as results of the five-year relationship.Flutie claimed it began working with Ayesha in Nov. 2014, when she had a much smaller social media and food-blog presence. The company alleged that its work helped turn her food interests into a larger entertainment and business career.The company alleged that Curry ended the relationship in May 2019. It claimed that she later denied Flutie its share of proceeds from businesses and slowed down new projects.Flutie also alleged that Curry hired a former employee of the company who had worked on her account. In the lawsuit, the company claimed Curry had “essentially gutted and devalued Flutie Entertainment’s interests.”Two ventures featured heavily in the complaint: Homemade, a planned home meal-kit and kitchen lifestyle business, and Yardie Girl, an entertainment production company.Flutie alleged that it had worked on partnerships, sponsors and the legal and financial structure surrounding Homemade. It also claimed involvement in developing Yardie Girl before Curry ended the relationship.The company sought at least $10 million in damages. It also asked for a ruling that would protect its claimed stake in Homemade and Yardie Girl.Flutie described itself as “clearly and undeniably instrumental in helping her achieve success.” That was the company’s position in the lawsuit and was not a finding by a court.Lawsuit highlighted Ayesha Curry's rise beyond Stephen Curry's fameThe legal dispute also put the spotlight on how quickly Curry had developed her own public profile.Curry was an actress before she married Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry in 2011. She began posting cooking demonstrations on YouTube in 2014 and later built a career around food, television and business.Flutie’s lawsuit, however, presented a different account of that rise. The company claimed Curry had a relatively modest social media and food-blog following when their relationship began and argued that its work played a major role in developing her business success.The lawsuit also claimed that Curry was known largely as Stephen Curry’s wife when Flutie first began working with her. That claim became part of the company’s argument that its involvement helped develop her independent business profile.Curry’s attorney Michael Plonsker rejected the allegations. He said Curry had ended her relationship with Robert Flutie in early 2019 and described him as a “disgruntled manager.”“We are confident that the legal process will find his accusations nonsensical and completely unfounded,” Plonsker said at the time.Curry’s legal team later challenged the case through the California Labor Commission, arguing that the commission had exclusive jurisdiction over the dispute. In a filing, Plonsker alleged that Flutie had viewed Curry as its “golden goose” and used “every manipulative and deceptive tactic” to seek larger shares of her earnings.Those statements came from Curry’s attorney and were allegations in the legal dispute, not findings by a court.The lawsuit came during a period when Curry and Stephen Curry were also involved in charitable efforts in the San Francisco Bay Area. The couple worked with the Alameda County Community Food Bank during the coronavirus pandemic to help provide one million meals to students affected by school closures.“We want to make sure that we rally around everyone and that these kids are not wondering where their next meal is coming from,” Ayesha Curry said about the food effort.The legal complaint, however, focused on a business disagreement and had no connection to the couple’s charitable work.The allegations in the lawsuit also did not establish that Curry had actually breached the agreement. Flutie presented its claims, while Curry’s legal team disputed them.The case later took another turn. In June 2021, a Los Angeles Superior Court judge put the civil lawsuit on hold after both sides agreed that proceedings should wait until the Labor Commission addressed Curry’s petition.Flutie Entertainment subsequently filed papers seeking dismissal of the lawsuit. By July 2021, the company had dropped the breach-of-contract case, although the broader dispute was still set to continue before a state Labor Commission officer.The dismissal did not amount to a court finding that Ayesha Curry had breached the agreement. articles.title: O que define um colchão de alto padrão? King Koil apresenta o conceito | G1
articles.standfirst: A escolha do colchão pode transformar a qualidade do sono e o bem-estar. Partindo desse princípio, a King Koil apresenta modelos premium, cada um com uma assinatura de conforto.
articles.summary: A escolha do colchão pode transformar a qualidade do sono e o bem-estar. Partindo desse princípio, a King Koil apresenta modelos premium, cada um com uma assinatura de conforto.
articles.body:
O que define um colchão de alto padrão? King Koil apresenta o conceito "Fator K” — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação.

A King Koil, fabricante global de colchões de luxo premium, lança neste mês a campanha Fator K no mercado brasileiro, para orientar a busca por noites de descanso verdadeiramente reparadoras. Por meio de tecnologias e de uma seleção criteriosa de matérias-primas, a marca demonstra como a escolha inteligente de um colchão de alto padrão eleva a experiência de dormir bem. A iniciativa destaca a combinação única de fatores que posicionam a marca em um patamar inimitável de colchões no país.

O que é o Fator K da King Koil e por que ele convida você a redefinir o modo de dormir bem?

Fundada em 1898, a marca americana desenvolve e testa seus sistemas de descanso de alta performance nos Estados Unidos. Atualmente, a sede mundial da empresa está localizada em Avondale, no Arizona. Com uma trajetória marcada pela busca constante por inovação, a King Koil consolidou sua presença global e tornou-se referência em conforto e tecnologia aplicada ao sono.

Ao transformar atributos de elevado padrão em benefícios perceptíveis no dia a dia, a marca traduz o conceito do quiet luxury para a rotina da casa. A tecnologia ganha evidência nos modelos Experience, Latex Selection, Crystal, Marble, Amethyst e SLX 435 , apresentados como os grandes destaques da vez. Dessa forma, cada pessoa encontra a combinação ideal entre colchões firmes, intermediários e macios.

Na prática, essa combinação une o melhor dos dois mundos. Afinal, os materiais certos ajudam a aliviar os pontos de pressão no corpo durante a noite. Ao mesmo tempo, você transforma o momento de dormir em um verdadeiro ritual de bem-estar, garantindo acordar com a energia renovada todos os dias.

O Fator K como expressão de qualidade no dia a dia

O conceito de quiet luxury prioriza a sofisticação discreta e o bem-estar genuíno. Na prática, essa percepção se reflete na escolha de itens que entregam conforto real e duradouro, onde a qualidade dos materiais fala mais alto do que o excesso visual.

A premissa de que "cada King Koil carrega seu próprio Fator K" dialoga diretamente com as exigências da rotina moderna. Seja para acompanhar uma rotina intensa de trabalho ou para garantir vitalidade ao longo dos anos, o alinhamento postural correto durante o sono renova a disposição física para o dia seguinte. Assim, a escolha por um colchão de alto padrão torna-se uma decisão natural de quem valoriza o autocuidado e a atenção aos detalhes.

Tecnologia e qualidade que sustentam o Fator K

A King Koil combina tradição, inovação e engenharia aplicada ao sono. Seus colchões incorporam tecnologias como o Far Infrared , que utiliza ondas de infravermelho longo para contribuir com o bem-estar durante o descanso, e o sistema Tri Support Zoned® , desenvolvido para oferecer sustentação diferenciada em regiões estratégicas do corpo. É também a única marca reconhecida pela dupla chancela do Instituto da Coluna Vertebral (ICV) e da Quiropraxia Brasil , além de contar com a certificação do INMETRO e o Selo ABICOL , reforçando seu compromisso com conforto, segurança e desempenho.

Destaques do Fator K para transformar o seu quarto

Agora que você já entende como o Fator K une a tradição centenária da King Koil ao cuidado com o sono, vale a pena conhecer de perto os modelos que lideram essa nova fase. Afinal, como cada pessoa busca uma experiência única ao deitar, apresentamos os detalhes das opções em evidência para ajudar você a escolher a sua:

Crystal: acolhimento em múltiplas camadas

O Fator K do Crystal está em sua construção sofisticada. O exclusivo Triple Encased Coil System reúne micromolas que acompanham os contornos do corpo e ampliam a capacidade de adaptação do colchão. O resultado é uma sensação de acolhimento preciso, sustentada por uma estrutura desenvolvida para quem busca conforto em seu nível mais elevado.

Experience: uma experiência de conforto envolvente

No Experience, o Fator K se revela na combinação entre um Pillow Top de proporções generosas e tecnologias exclusivas King Koil. Suas camadas foram desenvolvidas para criar uma superfície profundamente acolhedora, sem abrir mão do suporte. É uma escolha para quem deseja transformar o quarto em um espaço particular de conforto, sofisticação e bem-estar.

SLX 435: tecnologia para um descanso mais fresco

O Fator K do SLX 435 é o equilíbrio térmico. A malha IceTouch proporciona uma sensação refrescante ao contato, enquanto o Latex Gel Infused combina a elasticidade do látex com a ação refrescante do gel. A estrutura com molas ensacadas Contour Elite completa a experiência, oferecendo adaptação individualizada e estabilidade. Uma combinação indicada para quem valoriza o frescor, conforto e tecnologia durante toda a noite.

Amethyst: conforto equilibrado e acabamento refinado

O Fator K do Amethyst está na seleção criteriosa de matérias-primas e na presença do látex natural. Reconhecido por sua elasticidade e capacidade de resposta, o material acompanha os movimentos do corpo e contribui para uma sensação de conforto equilibrada. O toque suave e o acabamento refinado completam a proposta de um colchão criado para quem reconhece o luxo na origem e na qualidade de cada elemento.

Marble: maciez envolvente com sustentação precisa

No Marble, o Fator K está na combinação entre maciez e sustentação. Seu toque suave proporciona uma sensação de acolhimento profundo, enquanto a tecnologia Center Third Zoned reforça o terço central do colchão, região que concentra maior peso. O resultado é um conforto envolvente, com suporte equilibrado durante toda a noite.

Latex Selection: adaptação natural ao corpo

Por fim, o Fator K no modelo Latex Selection está na combinação entre Natural Latex e Memory Biofoam®, que acompanham os contornos do corpo e contribuem para uma distribuição equilibrada da pressão. O resultado é um conforto anatômico e acolhedor, aliado ao suporte preciso de uma estrutura de alto padrão.

Como a escolha do colchão premium certo pode transformar suas noites

A ciência do sono mostra que um descanso insuficiente ou de baixa qualidade pode afetar atenção, memória, tomada de decisões e desempenho durante o dia. Estudos também indicam que a superfície de descanso e o ambiente térmico podem influenciar o conforto e a qualidade percebida do sono. É nesse ponto que a escolha do colchão ganha relevância. Mais do que aliviar pontos de pressão, uma superfície de descanso de alto padrão deve oferecer sustentação compatível com o corpo, estabilidade durante as mudanças de posição e condições térmicas mais agradáveis. Para casais, a redução da transferência de movimentos também contribui para que a movimentação de uma pessoa interfira menos no descanso da outra.

Nos colchões King Koil, esses princípios orientam a combinação entre sistemas de molas de alta performance, espumas de alta qualidade, tecnologias de controle térmico e estruturas desenvolvidas para oferecer suporte em regiões estratégicas. Cada modelo reúne esses recursos de uma maneira particular, criando diferentes experiências de conforto sem perder a precisão técnica que caracteriza a marca.

Por isso, escolher um King Koil não se resume à estética ou à sensação percebida no primeiro contato. Significa encontrar uma composição de tecnologias adequada ao biotipo, à posição de dormir, à preferência de conforto e à rotina de quem irá utilizá-lo. Essa atenção individual é o que transforma a engenharia aplicada ao sono em uma experiência verdadeiramente premium.

Como vivenciar a experiência Fator K e transformar o seu sono?

Escolher um King Koil é ter acesso a mais de um século de conhecimento dedicado ao desenvolvimento de colchões e experiências de descanso de alto padrão. Desde 1898, a marca combina tradição internacional, seleção criteriosa de materiais e tecnologias desenvolvidas para atender diferentes biotipos e preferências. É essa bagagem histórica que sustenta a autoridade da fabricante no segmento e consolida o ato de dormir bem como um pilar fundamental da saúde física e mental.

O Fator K traduz justamente essa essência, uma assinatura exclusiva presente em todo o portfólio da marca. Então, para compreender esse diferencial na rotina, vivenciar a sensação de suporte do colchão é um passo essencial. As linhas da marca estão disponíveis em revendedores autorizados de todo o país, onde consultores orientam a escolha com base nas necessidades individuais. Informações sobre os produtos e a localização das lojas também podem ser encontradas no site oficial da King Koil Brasil ( kingkoil.com.br ).

Dê o próximo passo e descubra a experiência King Koil perto de você

Algumas escolhas podem ser explicadas. Outras precisam ser sentidas. Encontrar o colchão ideal envolve conhecer suas tecnologias, compreender seus diferenciais e, principalmente, perceber como cada composição responde ao seu corpo e às suas preferências de conforto.

O convite para redefinir o seu sono já está feito. Não adie a oportunidade de transformar cada momento em uma experiência memorável de absoluto bem-estar físico. Para explorar a campanha acompanhe as redes sociais da King Koil Brasil para se inspirar com novidades de design contemporâneo. Permita-se vivenciar o Fator K hoje mesmo e descubra como uma marca de prestígio internacional pode elevar a sua qualidade de vida.

Porque cada King Koil carrega seu próprio Fator K. E existe um deles esperando para transformar a sua forma de descansar.

articles.title: NBA: Michael Jordan 'Last Dance' jersey sells for £9m
articles.summary: A Michael Jordan jersey from his 'Last Dance' season sells for $12.3m, a record for a piece of Jordan memorabilia.
articles.body:
A Michael Jordan jersey from his 'Last Dance' season has sold for $12.3m (£9.3m), a record for a piece of game-worn Jordan memorabilia.

He wore the jersey in game three of the 1998 NBA Finals, his last season with the Chicago Bulls.

Jordan helped the Bulls win the series 4-2 for his sixth and final NBA Championship. He was named the Finals' Most Valuable Player in all six.

The previous record for a piece of Jordan memorabilia was $10.1m (£7.6m) for his jersey from game one of the 1998 Finals.

The game three jersey was put up for sale by entrepreneur Ryan Gough and sold at Joopiter, Pharrell Williams' digital auction house, which gave it an estimated price of $10-15m (£7.5-£11.3m).

Jordan's 1997 Ferrari 550 Maranello was sold for $2.7m (£2m), four times the auction record for that model.

"Few objects in the history of sport embody greatness as completely as Michael Jordan's game three jersey from the 1998 NBA Finals," Joopiter said in the auction posting.

"Worn during the Last Dance... it marks the culmination of an era that transformed basketball into a global cultural phenomenon.

"Today it stands among the most important game-worn sports artifacts ever to come to market."

The record price for a piece of game-worn sports memorabilia is the jersey worn by baseball legend Babe Ruth when he "called the shot" during the 1932 World Series, which was sold for $24.1m (£18.2m) in 2024.

articles.title: El Real Madrid, a evitar el peor inicio europeo de su historia
articles.standfirst: Tras caer ante Dubai y Efes podría ponerse 0-3 si pierde hoy en su visita al Hapoel Tel Aviv. Lo nunca visto en el club blanco desde que se creó la Copa de Europa hace 68 años
articles.summary: Tras caer ante Dubai y Efes podría ponerse 0-3 si pierde hoy en su visita al Hapoel Tel Aviv. Lo nunca visto en el club blanco desde que se creó la Copa de Europa hace 68 años
articles.body: Hace apenas 12 días el Real Madrid conquistó la SuperCup de la Euroliga, el primer título de la temporada, pero su dubitativo inicio en la Liga Endesa, con remontada milagrosa en casa ante el Unicaja, y sobre todo sus dos derrotas en la Euroliga en cancha del Dubai (78-77) y del Anadolu Efes (94-84), han difuminado la alegría de ese título de la cabeza de sus seguidores y le han colocado en una situación peliaguda pese a que en ambos partidos compitió y pudo ganar. Esta tarde afronta su tercera salida seguida en la no menos complicada cancha del Hapoel Tel Aviv en su exilio en Sofía. Si pierde establecería con 0-3 el peor inicio continental de su historia en 68 años, desde que tomó parte en la primera Copa de Europa creada en 1958. Hasta ahora sus peores arranques continentales habían sido en la 1999-00, cuando perdió de inicio con el Olimpia Ljubljana y el Zalgiris; y en la 2020-21 tras caer ante Baskonia y Valencia. El calendario está jugando en su contra al tener que afrontar tres salidas ante tres candidatos a entrar en los playoffs. Y pese a lo incipiente de la temporada una tercera derrota puede empezar a impacientar a sus aficionados e incluso a sus dirigentes. La paciencia en un club como el Madrid tiene un límite muy pequeño. En esta tesitura aparece en escena un Hapoel Tel Aviv que se estrenó con derrota ante el Bayern (84-86) y luego ganó fuera al Estrella Roja (80-81). Los de Itoudis, con Micic, Bryant, Blakeney, Oturu, Ennis, Satoransky o Leday son una amenaza de primer orden.

articles.title: Así elegirá la Euroliga a sus nuevos socios: 11 candidatos para 8 plazas
articles.standfirst: Competitividad, solvencia, mercado, dinero y reputación, principales factores para incorporar a ocho franquicias nuevas. El Valencia pasa la primera criba y tiene muchas opciones
articles.summary: Competitividad, solvencia, mercado, dinero y reputación, principales factores para incorporar a ocho franquicias nuevas. El Valencia pasa la primera criba y tiene muchas opciones
articles.body: La Euroliga, independientemente de que la NBA la haga llegar alguna oferta que considere interesante para unirse a su proyecto y formar una alianza común, sigue adelante con su imparable transición hacia un sistema cerrado de franquicias, proceso capital en su ambicioso plan de expansión. En los últimos meses, semanas e incluso días ha recibido al menos dos docenas de ofertas vinculantes de equipos e inversores deseosos de unirse a su proyecto. Y ahora llega el momento de elegir a sus nuevos socios, algo que harán el lunes y martes próximos en la Asamblea General que celebrarán en el Lago Como y que contará con la presencia de los accionistas dueños de la competición. Los últimos en mostrar su interés a través de una oferta han sido el Aris Salónica y el Zenit San Petersburgo, en el caso de los rusos para cuando acabe el conflicto bélico con Ucrania. Ahora serán los 13 clubes propietarios de la Euroliga, Real Madrid, Barcelona y Baskonia (España), Panathinaikos y Olympiacos (Grecia), Anadolu Efes y Fenerbahçe (Turquía), Armani Milan (Italia), Maccabi Tel Aviv (Israel), Zalgiris Kaunas (Lituania), Bayern Munich (Alemania), ASVEL Villeurbanne (Francia) y CSKA Moscú (Rusia), los que elegirán a ocho franquiciados entre las 11 candidaturas que ya han superado el primer corte. Valencia Basket, Virtus Bolonia, París Basketball, Hapoel Tel Aviv, Estrella Roja, Partizan, PAOK, Napoli, Dubai Basketball, London Lions y Maxima Roma ya han hecho los deberes. Y Hapoel Jerusalem, Aris Salónica, Besiktas y Zenit San Petersburgo han solicitado también poder entrar en el proceso de selección. Ahora llega lo más difícil: decidir cuáles son los ocho proyectos que mejor representan la Euroliga del futuro. Un dilema complicado para la organización dadas las altas capacidades de los candidatos. La Euroliga y sus accionistas, en contra de lo que algunos podrían pensar, no tomarán su decisión basándose exclusivamente en los criterios económicos. Siendo estos importantes, sería de necios negarlo, no será sólo una cuestión de quién pone más dinero sobre la mesa. La organización quiere proyectos sostenibles a largo plazo y, para ello, está sometiendo a los aspirantes a una segunda y definitiva ‘due diligence’, una auditoria exhaustiva de sus propuestas para verificar la veracidad de su información y detectar riesgos. El primer criterio será el deportivo. La Euroliga analizará el nivel competitivo de cada club, su trayectoria, su estructura, sus resultados y, especialmente, su capacidad para mantenerse en la élite. No basta con tener un gran proyecto económico: la competición quiere equipos capaces de competir y de elevar el nivel y el grado de exigencia inherente desde hace años a la propia Euroliga. También pesará, y mucho, quién está detrás de cada candidatura. La propiedad, sus recursos, su estabilidad y la solvencia real del proyecto estarán bajo la lupa. La Euroliga quiere conocer hasta el último detalle de los grupos que aspiran a convertirse en accionistas y asegurarse de que existe músculo financiero suficiente para sostener inversiones millonarias durante muchos años. La reputación será otro factor determinante. La organización estudiará el historial de cada club, su credibilidad institucional, su comportamiento y su imagen dentro y fuera de la cancha. Una franquicia no sólo debe aportar dinero y jugadores: debe ser un socio fiable para el resto de accionistas y contribuir a fortalecer la marca Euroliga. El cuarto gran elemento será el mercado que pueda generar cada candidatura. La ciudad, su población, su potencial económico, su capacidad de atraer aficionados y patrocinadores y la posibilidad de abrir nuevos territorios serán variables esenciales. Londres, por ejemplo, representa una oportunidad estratégica en un mercado todavía por conquistar, mientras Italia, Grecia o Francia ofrecen plazas con una enorme tradición baloncestística. La masa social y el impacto mediático tampoco serán secundarios. Tener aficionados, llenar pabellones, generar audiencia, atraer patrocinadores y despertar interés más allá de la propia ciudad será una carta fundamental. La Euroliga busca clubes que puedan convertirse en auténticos motores de crecimiento y que aporten seguidores nuevos a la competición. Y aquí aparece una de las claves del proceso: el canon de franquicia no será necesariamente decisivo. Aunque las 11 ofertas vinculantes finalistas suman cerca de 700 millones de euros (añadiendo algunas de última hora pueden llegar a 1.000), la Euroliga no pretende adjudicar las plazas simplemente a quien pague más. El precio deberá guardar relación con la calidad global del proyecto y con lo que cada candidato pueda aportar al futuro de la competición. Con todos esos elementos sobre la mesa, la segunda ‘due diligence’ será un examen final. Deportivo, económico, propiedad, reputación, mercado, aficionados y capacidad de crecimiento conformarán el cóctel que valorará la Euroliga para decidir quién entra y quién se queda fuera. Las deliberaciones finales están teniendo lugar ahora y la decisión definitiva de los elegidos se conocerá durante la Asamblea General que celebrarán el lunes y el martes en el marco incomparable del Lago de Como (Italia).

articles.title: Who is A'ja Wilson? WNBA star who confronted an Indiana Fever fan at a playoff game
articles.summary: A'ja Wilson confronted a fan pointing at her during the Aces vs Fever game, earning a technical foul but standing firmly behind her reaction.
articles.body: A'ja Wilson didn't give a damn. When she saw "a man" pointing at her, she approached him, pointed back and exchanged words, before teammates and arena personnel pulled her away. She received a technical foul for unsportsmanlike conduct, while the fan was initially escorted from his seat. Arena security later interviewed the fan and nearby witnesses and determined that he had not violated the Fever’s Fan Code of Conduct. He was allowed to return to his seat, reportedly to applause and high-fives from the home crowd. But Wilson stood behind her reaction after the game. "If I see a man come at me, taking steps toward me and pointing at me, I don’t give a damn what you said," Wilson told reporters. "I don’t give a damn how you said it, the tone. That is unacceptable. You don’t step towards me — you never should — and point at me. I’m not for that s--- at all." JEMELE HILL SAYS WE CAN'T BLAME A'JA WILSON FOR CHARGING AT FANS BECAUSE OF WHAT 'MEN' HAVE DONE And just like that, the WNBA had its next dramatic episode in a long-running series of such episodes in the 2026 season. So who exactly is the WNBA legend who didn’t give a damn on Tuesday night? THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Forged in faith, music and a military background A’ja Riyadh Wilson was born Aug. 8, 1996, and raised just outside Columbia, South Carolina, by Roscoe and Eva Wilson. Her distinctive first name originated with her father’s taste in music. Roscoe, who played professional basketball in Europe, attended a Steely Dan concert overseas and decided that if he ever had a daughter, he would name her after the band’s 1977 song and album "Aja." Her middle name, Riyadh, came from the capital of Saudi Arabia, where her maternal aunt was stationed during Operation Desert Storm, per NBC Olympics. Christianity and church life were fixtures of Wilson’s upbringing. Her paternal grandfather, Roscoe Wilson Sr., served as a minister at Saint John Baptist Church in Columbia for approximately 50 years, while her grandmother was a missionary. Wilson grew up attending the church and has credited its congregation and the surrounding community with helping raise her, per NBC Sports. Wilson recalled that Saint John had a children’s church and that she sometimes chased other children around the pews. Basketball was not initially part of Wilson’s plan. Despite her father’s playing career and her older brother’s interest in the sport, she gravitated toward activities such as soccer, volleyball, ballet and piano. She later joked that she "was not a girly that liked to sweat." ""I was not a girly that liked to sweat. Now, I sweat for a living, and it pays my bills," Wilson told TIME in 2025. Wilson attended Heathwood Hall Episcopal School, a predominantly White private school where she struggled to fit in socially and academically. She has written that classmates directed racial comments at her and made her feel different because she was Black, in The Players’ Tribune. She was also diagnosed with dyslexia during her sophomore year of high school after years of struggling to process large blocks of text. Wilson later wrote that she dreaded being asked to read a pregame Psalm aloud more than playing in front of a hostile crowd. The experience eventually inspired her foundation’s work supporting children with dyslexia and combating bullying. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM VS DIJONAI CARRINGTON: HOW TWO EX-FOOTBALL PLAYERS COLLIDED IN THE 'PRIVILEGE' DEBATE Her father started taking her to the gym for early-morning and weekend workouts, setting her on the path from reluctant basketball player to the nation’s top high school recruit. Wilson has frequently discussed race While sitting courtside with then-Las Vegas Aces teammate Kelsey Plum at the 2024 Final Four, Wilson turned a conversation about UConn star Paige Bueckers into a racial discussion. "Us, as Black women, Paige reminds me a lot of you," Wilson told Plum. "She knows how her privilege has gotten her to that point. And also, like, she’s good at basketball. She understands her privilege. It’s like what pushes her over the top, in a sense. It reminds me a lot of you." In 2020, Wilson became one of the players selected to lead the newly created WNBA/WNBPA Social Justice Council. The league dedicated that season to racial-justice causes following the deaths of George Floyd and Breonna Taylor, placing "Black Lives Matter" on its courts and Taylor’s name on players’ jerseys as part of the "Say Her Name" campaign. After a Kentucky grand jury declined to charge any officers directly in Taylor’s death, Wilson called the decision a "slap on the wrist, and invoked the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks. "People remember exactly where they were when 9/11 happened or when other things happened. This is my 9/11. ... I was too young [for that]; I was in preschool [in 2001]. But this here is going to be something I remember all the time. I have to fear for my life as a Black woman, whether I'm asleep, I'm awake, whether I am walking down the street. Justice was not served, and that just really broke my heart." Wilson said, per ESPN. The article was published 13 days after the 19th anniversary of 9/11. Wilson also published an essay titled "Dear Black Girls" in 2020, describing the racism and isolation she experienced while attending a predominantly White private school. She wrote that her broader purpose was to assure young Black girls that they were seen, heard and capable of making an impact. "This isn’t just a hashtag," she wrote in the Player's Tribune essay ahead of the 2020 season. "We’re all in it and we demand change." Her activism extended into electoral politics during the same season. WNBA players publicly opposed then-Atlanta Dream co-owner and Republican Sen. Kelly Loeffler after Loeffler criticized the league’s embrace of Black Lives Matter. Players wore "Vote Warnock" shirts supporting Democratic challenger Raphael Warnock, who later defeated Loeffler in Georgia’s Senate runoff. Wilson’s Social Justice Council also held discussions about voting rights, LGBTQ advocacy and gun control. Wilson has continued to argue that Black women must work harder to receive the same recognition as others. In a 2024 ESPN interview, she said Black girls are often taught that they must work "10 times as hard just to get a foot in the door." She has built one of the most decorated résumés in basketball history Wilson’s basketball résumé includes success at every level. At South Carolina, she became the first three-time SEC Player of the Year and led the Gamecocks to their first national championship in 2017. She was named the Final Four’s Most Outstanding Player that year before sweeping the major national player-of-the-year awards as a senior. Wilson finished her college career as South Carolina’s all-time leader in points and blocked shots. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The Las Vegas Aces selected her with the first overall pick in the 2018 WNBA Draft, and she immediately won Rookie of the Year. Wilson has since captured a record four league MVP awards and four Defensive Player of the Year honors, including a share of the defensive award in 2025. Wilson led Las Vegas to WNBA championships in 2022, 2023 and 2025, earning Finals MVP honors in the latter two title runs. Entering the 2026 season, she ranked first in WNBA history in career scoring average and first in 30-point double-doubles. She has also won two Olympic gold medals with Team USA, starting for the Americans at both the Tokyo and Paris Games. Wilson added another honor in September 2026 when the Associated Press named her its WNBA Player of the Year for the third consecutive season. What comes next? Wilson and the Aces will have little time to dwell on the confrontation. Las Vegas will host Indiana in a winner-take-all Game 3 Thursday at 9 p.m. ET. The game will air on USA Network and CNBC, with the winner advancing to the WNBA semifinals and the loser’s season coming to an immediate end. The teams have already traded decisive victories. Wilson overwhelmed Indiana with 38 points and 16 rebounds in Las Vegas’ 102-85 Game 1 win, but Caitlin Clark answered with 27 points and 15 assists as the Fever won Game 2, 99-89. Wilson finished the loss with 22 points and nine rebounds, while her fourth-quarter confrontation became the game’s defining controversy. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Now, Wilson will return to a friendly Las Vegas crowd with an opportunity to redirect the conversation. A dominant Game 3 would move the defending champions one step closer to their fourth title in five seasons. A loss would end their reign—and ensure that Wilson’s final act of the postseason included charging into the stands to confront a fan.

articles.title: Ranking Every NBA Team's Starting Lineup Ahead of Preseason
articles.summary: On the NBA calendar, October is a month of unbridled optimism.
articles.body:
On the NBA calendar, October is a month of unbridled optimism.

Especially at the start when everyone has the same record, and a huge chunk of the league is purportedly in the best shape of their lives.

It's also a time to reset the landscape. Three-plus months have passed since the last champion was crowned, and it honestly feels like longer given how much has changed between now and then.

So, we're here to predict and rank each starting lineup with the dust all but settled on the offseason. We won't magically heal any injured players or include any unsigned players (cough, Jalen Duren ), but we will peer into our trusty crystal ball to project how any new additions will fit their teams.

The Giannis Antetokounmpo-less Bucks are starting from scratch, creating plenty of fluidity with the first five. With a fair share of veteran holdovers and young talent sure to be promoted upon the first hints of readiness, this is a lineup that could change looks over and over.

For now, though, this feels like the right starting point. Herro has been an All-Star before, and Rollins had a Most Improved Player award argument last season. They should comprise the opening-night starting backcourt, although lottery pick Brayden Burries will have ample opportunity to challenge for his spot.

Up front, Milwaukee might love to see Kel'el Ware and Nate Ament force their way into this five, but that's probably more of a midseason development than an October occurrence. Jaquez, Kuzma and Turner will all have chances to showcase themselves for potential trade-season suitors.

While optimism should run in near limitless supply this time of the year, it'll be tough for Sacramento fans to summon.

LaVine and Sabonis would be gone already if they had a trade market. The same almost certainly applies to Hunter, and Murray keeps moving further away from the buzz that accompanied his arrival as the No. 4 pick of the 2022 draft.

Acuff, then, might be solely responsible for inspiring hope here—as a 19-year-old who averaged nearly as many shots as points and turnovers as assists at summer league. Efficiency figures to be a struggle, but even his volume is far from guaranteed with those veterans needing touches to try attracting any external interest.

Considering how long it was apparent that a rebuild was inevitable in Chicago, the Bulls are almost unforgivably light on young talent. Luckily, though, they've seemingly guessed right on both Buzelis and Wilson, who already comprise one of the Association's most intriguing young forward tandems.

That said, unless the youngsters are way ahead of schedule, there is a distinct lack of star power with this group. Powell at least earned an All-Star nod last season, but that was the first selection of his now 12-year career, and his production plummeted after the break. He's also on the short list of the league's most obvious trade candidates as a 33-year-old starter on a long-term rebuilder.

Giddey can stuff a stat sheet (17 points, 9.1 assists and 8.3 rebounds last season), but his limitations as a shooter and defender render him less helpful on the hardwood than those numbers suggest ( minus-2.1 career net differential). Claxton's defensive playmaking has really regressed, and on offense, he lacks shooting from the perimeter and size on the interior.

Dillon Brooks Charged with DUI from March Arrest (AP)

NBA Trade To Boost a New Eastern Conference Contender 🏀

Grizzlies fans won't love this ranking—but they might begrudgingly get it.

Boozer might have the polish and production of a plug-and-play pro, but he's still an unproven 19-year-old awaiting his first career minutes. Edey's apparent sophomore leap spanned only 11 games before an ankle injury ended his run. Coward cracked the All-Rookie first team, but he might be more solid than special.

After that, Jerome and Grant are neither needle-movers, nor guaranteed starters. The former will be pushed by Scottie Pippen Jr., while the latter—a clear trade candidate—could be challenged by Jaylen Wells, if only for the fact that he has a clearer future with the franchise.

There might be disconnected timelines and competitions for touches here, but there could also be a (relatively) good amount of talent.

Randle has previously booked multiple All-Star trips, Porter posted All-Star numbers last season and the Brown-Dëmin backcourt looked as electric as any on this year's summer circuit. Sharpe's per-minute production suggests he could factor into the Most Improved Player race with a big spike in floor time after Nic Claxton's exit.

Brooklyn probably still isn't a Play-In Tournament factor, and there's surely a price point at which the Nets would deal just about any veteran for assets, but this quintet could look competent if Brown and Dëmin are ready to roll.

The Kawhi Leonard-less Clippers appeared undermanned even before Brandon Ingram was lost to a partial Achilles tear . But that news torpedoed any chances L.A. may have had of escaping the bottom third.

Things aren't entirely hopeless, though. The Garland-Wagler backcourt should provide plenty of potency and creativity, provided the former can stay healthy and the latter can hit the ground running.

If the guards are good, the frontcourt should be fine. Strus, Hachimura and Lopez have all started for playoff teams in the past. Maybe that's a reason for some win-now shopper to make a run at them, but given L.A.'s glaring need for assets , that would be a welcome development.

The Hornets aren't the easiest team to rank, since there are ways to paint this as unfair in either direction.

On one hand, this is far from a favorable placement for a club that posted the NBA's best net rating from Jan. 1 through the end of last regular season. On the other, it might be a bit generous for a group that will have to forge its identity on the fly while replacing former franchise face LaMelo Ball and longtime starter Miles Bridges.

The wager here is that Knueppel and Miller both take significant steps forward while seizing more control of the offense, while White and Reid take advantage of their promotions to full-time starters.

Diabaté's spot might be the shakiest, but that's only because Charlotte has viable alternatives in Ryan Kalkbrenner and rookie lottery pick Hannes Steinbach.

The Pelicans have enough talent to push for a higher spot, but a good chunk of that talent has been present for a while now, and this club still has 117 losses to show for the last two seasons.

Health is forever a question mark for this club, but so is overall performance. Williamson isn't where he wants to be , Murphy's biggest numbers have come on brutally bad teams and Murray's lone All-Star nod in 2022 feels forever ago.

It's uncertain how the rest of the opening group will take shape since multiple reasonable candidates (like Jeremiah Fears, Saddiq Bey, Bennedict Mathurin and Yves Missi) were left on the cutting room floor.

If this is how new coach Jamahl Mosley chooses to open games, there will be immediate concerns about perimeter shooting and interior defense.

Curry might be one of hoops history's greatest magicians, but even he'll struggle to work miracles with this already injury-riddled roster . Especially if the knee problems that plagued the 38-year-old last season prove problematic once again.

If this is the best Dubs can do for now, things could unravel before they ever get whole. Podziemski is over his skis as a second option, Santos has to hustle his way into glue-guy capacity and the interior combo of Green and Horford is ancient and borderline punchless on offense.

It would still be tough to slot a lineup featuring Curry any lower, but a squad that once touted its strength in numbers feels frighteningly close to being a one-man show.

The Mavs have long signaled their excitement to see Irving and Flagg together, and we're right there with them. The wide gap in timelines figures probably points toward an eventual split, but there could be a lot of fun basketball between now and then.

Flagg was forced to take a lot of tough shots last season, and that burden should be immediately eased by Irving's improvisation, spacing and scoring. If this on-court pairing even approaches its on-paper potential, then the support starters shouldn't have trouble completing the puzzle.

All of that said, there's a chance Flagg is the only Dallas starter who makes it to season's end. Suitors are already circling Irving, they could come for Washington pretty quickly and Gafford would be expendable if Dereck Lively II ever gets healthy .

Christie, 23, could be a long-term keeper, but his ceiling doesn't sit high enough for the Mavericks to treat him as totally off-limits should someone present an aggressive offer.

The Suns surprised and probably overachieved last season—while winning 45 games and finishing 15th in net rating. Their ceiling only stretches so high as a one-star squad, and, no, Bridges doesn't change that label despite Phoenix paying a star-type price to acquire him.

There are solid support pieces around Booker—though not as many as there would be with Mark Williams banged-up —but where is the second needle-mover?

Bridges and Green are inefficient scoring specialists, Brooks just had a career season on 54 percent true shooting (league average was 58.1 ) and Ighodoro is keeping the seat warm until Williams gets healthy or Khaman Maluach leaps forward.

It sounds like Portland plans on rolling with a Morant-Lillard combo in the backcourt, meaning the Blazers are cannonballing right into the too-many-cooks-in-the-kitchen concerns. Both are lead guards who do their best work with the ball in their hands, so the fit could be tricky from the start.

Never mind the obvious defensive concerns the pairing presents. Or the worries of what this might do to the on-ball opportunities that fueled Avdija's All-Star ascension last season. Or the fact that this arrangement could force Jrue Holiday to the bench, since the Blazers might view Camara's defense and Clingan's paint protection as absolute must-haves.

There is talent here, though, and maybe a good deal of it if Avdija picks up where he left off, Lillard shows no rust after a season-long layoff and Morant looks healthy and explosive. The puzzle pieces just don't obviously align and may never until Portland thins out its guard group.

This sentiment hasn't been raised in a while, and it may lead to eventual egg-on-face regret, but here it is: We are bullish on the Wizards. OK, maybe bullish is too strong of a term for a team coming off three consecutive 60-loss campaigns, but we're at least optimistically intrigued.

Washington needed an on-court organizer and found one of the league's most prolific playmakers in Young (career 9.8 assists). It lacked defensive protection on the back end and now has a five-time All-Defensive honoree back there in Davis. It looked short on star potential and then struck lottery gold with Dybantsa, the No. 1 pick of the celebrated and highly anticipated 2026 draft class.

This group obviously lacks a track record together, and the incumbents haven't spent an NBA second in a winning environment. Still, this squad is starting to make real sense, especially if Sarr and George can continue their ascensions from last season.

The Jazz share a host of similarities with the Wizards—including the recent tank jobs and new expectations surrounding recently acquired in-prime stars and the just-drafted blue-chip prospects—making it all the more appropriate to keep these clubs closely connected.

A direct Washington-vs-Utah assessment might be a coin flip, but Utah gets the slightest nod for being more proven on the court. Because the Jazz not only have a pair of prime stars in Markkanen and Jackson, they also have an ascending 22-year-old who has already authored a breakout in George.

Throw in Peterson as, at worst, a combo guard with impact at both ends and Nurkić as a dot-connecting bruiser and slick-passing center, and the pieces just align a tad more tightly.

With Suggs, Wagner and Banchero all residing in the 25-and-under tier, Orlando feels like it should have some unrealized potential. Yet, three consecutive first-round exits give the Magic much more of a plateaued appearance.

Maybe new coach Sean Sweeney can change that. Or perhaps it's just as simple as having everyone healthy at the same time.

It doesn't feel impossible for this club to flip the proverbial switch, but it clearly needs to happen sooner than later. This quintet might only be one sluggish start away from a significant shakeup.

Pistons fans might be in an uproar, as 15th is hardly a favorable perch to put a team coming off a 60-win campaign. However, these rankings reflect only the projected starters, not the team at large, and this group is notably lacking two things.

The first is would-be starter Jalen Duren, who still hasn't signed yet and is drumming up enough sign-and-trade interest to wonder whether his future will be spent elsewhere. Yes, even while the Pistons keep insisting that it won't .

The second is the still-missing second shot-creator who would immediately relieve some of the heavy burden being shouldered by Cunningham. In fact, this group might have even less creativity than it did before with self-sufficient scorer Tobias Harris, who had Detroit's second-most points in the playoffs, having been replaced with the play-finishing Collins.

At 36 years old with a couple of serious leg injuries in his past, Thompson's days of manning the 2 should probably be behind him. Yet, he was recently labeled "the leading candidate" for that exact starting spot by Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald , who cited the Heat's need for outside shooting as the primary rationale.

But regardless of whether the spot goes to Thompson, Tim Hardaway Jr. or even rookie Ryan Conwell, it seems earmarked for a shooting specialist with limited creation. And since the Heat aren't getting creation from Wiggins either, that puts a ton of pressure on Mitchell to keep improving as a playmaker and on coach Erik Spoelstra to bring the best out of his star bigs.

Speaking of, Antetokounmpo and Adebayo should be awesome together. Each possesses unfair versatility for someone with their size and strength, and they're both comfortable handling the ball and attacking downhill. Spacing remains an obvious (and maybe ominous) concern, but the star power still pushes Miami into the upper-half.

Dončić, Reaves and Kessler are starting-lineup locks. Little is known about who will fill the other two spots, beyond Redick's deadpan comment to reporters at media day that they "will not be two white guys."

Dončić and Reaves should rank among the most productive backcourts in basketball. They'll also comprise one of its most generous guard groups, too, which makes the interior presence of Kessler so critical to this club's success.

Those are three impact players, but the last two spots will lag behind regardless of how Redick fills them.

Grimes and LaRavia both have three-and-D traits that could make them the best complements, but if they were better fits for that role, this debate would have been settled already.

Without question, Boston stepped backward this summer. The question is just how much ground that retreat covered.

If Tatum returns to his old superstar form, and White rediscovers his shooting efficiency, then maybe it isn't much. But it's definitely some, as the Celtics replaced a 29-year-old MVP candidate in Jaylen Brown with a 36-year-old who last booked an All-Star trip in 2024—and played just 78 games the past two seasons combined—in George.

Coach Joe Mazzulla has other options to fill out his five, but Payton Pritchard and Mitchell Robinson might be best deployed off the bench. The Celtics might also prefer Scheierman's versatility over Sam Hauser's shooting.

The Pacers have an argument for a higher ranking than this. And it is a rather compelling one. Eighty percent of this lineup pushed the Oklahoma City Thunder to seven games in the 2025 NBA Finals, and the one who wasn't around for that run, Zubac, earned All-Defensive second-team honors that same season.

Still, it would be assuming quite a bit to think the Pacers can just jump back on the bicycle after everything that has changed since. Haliburton just lost an entire season to an Achilles tear suffered in Game 7 of that championship round, and while the early returns sound promising , there's no telling of whether he'll be as impactful after such a serious injury.

This group could also be a bit more squeezed for spacing. Zubac is an upgrade over Myles Turner in many respects, but long-range shooting is the obvious exception. And maybe it proves a big one if Siakam, a career 34.2 percent three-point shooter, can't consistently find his range.

The Hawks had a productive offseason, but they probably didn't nab a new starter over the offseason.

Lottery pick Kingston Flemings should eventually push for an opening role if everything goes right with his development, and Lu Dort's championship experience should earn him a nod, but Atlanta has had good success with this projected lineup.

Great success, actually. This fivesome logged nearly 400 minutes together last season and trounced opponents by 20.3 points per 100 possessions when it did.

That said, that successful run was a relatively short one (30 games), and it largely came against a favorable schedule down the stretch. It also failed to carry over to the playoffs, where this group had a minus-14.4 net rating across 82 minutes.

Throw in the lack of a certified superstar, and it would be harder to slot the Hawks any higher.

Minnesota has much more of a mystery-team feel than you'd expect from a club with 154 wins and five series victories to show for the past three seasons. But the Wolves may have reached identity-changing levels with their offseason adjustments, captured here by the additions of Ball and Kuminga.

They probably widened the gap between their best- and worst-case scenarios, but they probably made their offense more dynamic, too. Edwards told reporters he's "happy" to have Ball behind the wheel now and thinks the change could give him more fuel for the defensive end now.

The returning trio of Edwards, McDaniels and Gobert posted a plus-6.9 net rating over 1,007 minutes last season. That's a really good number, it's just not quite a great one. Minnesota clearly believes it has a higher gear it can reach. This ranking leaves that door open but stops well short of guaranteeing any breakthrough.

Leonard is back north of the border for a second stint with the Raptors and hoping history repeats itself. During his previous single-season tenure with the team, Toronto won 58 games and captured its only title in franchise history.

Asking for a repeat would be asking too much, but Toronto boasts a talented roster, and this fivesome shows it.

The Raptors have a legitimate go-to offensive option in Leonard now, plus an ascending co-star in Barnes. Quickley and Barrett both pack an offensive punch, and Poeltl is a capable anchor when his back isn't bothering him. This quintet could prove elite on defense and good-to-really-good on offense.

Was Houston's failure to launch last season really all about VanVleet's absence and the subsequent lack of an on-court conductor? Honestly, it could have been. The Rockets were atrocious in clutch situations, sitting 24th in net rating and 29th in turnover percentage—borderline impossibly awful numbers for a club with a closer like Durant.

With VanVleet's organizational skills, the Rockets can take full advantage of their talent level. That should mean cleaner looks—and, by extension, more efficiency—for everyone. It could also mean even more defensive activity for Thompson, who shouldn't be tasked with nearly as many playmaking duties.

This is all assuming, of course, that VanVleet, who turns 33 in February and lost last season to an ACL tear, is healthy now, stays that way all season and looks exactly how he did before the injury. Between that and the chances Houston's issues ran beyond the point guard spot, there are some reasons to be skeptical.

Did the Cavaliers finally do it? Was their aggressive sign-and-trade acquisition of Watson the attempt that solved their issue at small forward once and for all?

Cleveland staked plenty on that being the case, in terms of both the acquisition cost and the drained asset pool left behind. The Cavs will have nothing to regret if the wager hits, though. And it just might, given Watson's documented defensive impact and opportunity to continue his offensive ascension.

It's still fair to question the defensive viability of this backcourt and raise concerns over the frontcourt's lack of shooting, but it's also easy for the imagination to run wild should everything click. The sample size was tiny, but when the Cavs had Harden, Mitchell, Mobley and Allen together last season, they walloped opponents by 26.7 points per 100 possessions.

Like Michael Porter Jr. last offseason and Peyton Watson this summer, the Nuggets keep making financial squeezes that cost them talented players. And they might keep getting away with it, because Jokić, who has no interest in hooping elsewhere , is the NBA's resident rising tide lifting all boats around him.

"When you have the best player in the world, anything's possible," Nuggets newcomer DeMar DeRozan told reporters .

If Denver can keep everyone in this first five upright, it should have one of the league's top lineups. That's mostly because Jokić anchors it, but Murray is a legitimate co-star, and Gordon (when healthy) fills the perfect support role. Braun and Johnson are both in need of bounce-back efforts, but both have been helpful role players in the past.

Spurs coach Mitch Johnson has a wealth of talent at his disposal—and some difficult decisions as a result. It sure sounds like Dylan Harper feels ready and worthy of a starting spot, and a camp competition for a starting forward spot could include the likes of Keldon Johnson, Harrison Barnes and newcomer Tobias Harris.

What Johnson also has, though, is his most utilized starting five (and lineup overall ) from last season, when San Antonio reeled off 62 wins and pushed its way through to the NBA Finals.

If Johnson doesn't bother trying to fix something that obviously isn't broken, San Antonio might leave its opening quintet untouched (for now). The Spurs won 21 of the 24 games these five started together during the regular season, and they bettered opponents by 17.6 points per 100 possessions across their 284 minutes together.

With Oklahoma City coming off of consecutive 64-plus-win campaigns, you might think there would be nothing for head coach Mark Daigneault to figure out. But after tightening the budget this summer, the Thunder need a replacement for Lu Dort, a starting-lineup staple for the past six seasons.

Daigneault will choose between Wallace and Ajay Mitchell. Wallace, an All-Defensive second-teamer last season, is the cleanest stylistic replacement. If OKC wants more offensive oomph, though, Mitchell boasts the deeper bag as a scorer and shot-creator.

If Williams is healthy, though, the offense should be in great shape. That might nudge the needle toward Wallace, who could be similarly tenacious to Dort on the ball and more of a playmaker off of it (and still more threatening offensively).

Should the backbone of the reigning champs be automatically awarded the No. 1 spot? Maybe, but slotting New York above both San Antonio and Oklahoma City already feels like a hat-tip acknowledgment of that awesome run.

Before that run, this group was merely pretty good, posting a plus-2.3 net rating across 541 regular-season minutes. For context, that would have ranked 12th overall . In the postseason, though, this lineup became a statistical steamroller, pulverizing opponents by 12.5 points per 100 possessions, which would have easily ranked No. 1.

Did these five punch above their weight class? It's possible, but this lineup covers all of the bases you would want with an MVP candidate in Brunson, a skilled co-star in Towns, a couple of two-way support wings in Anunoby and Bridges, plus perhaps the league's ultimate glue guy in Hart.

The individual parts are all solid or better, but the chemistry and cohesiveness of the collective are what make the whole spectacular.

No, these Sixers haven't logged a single second together. And, sure, the lineup has a host of unanswered questions, like availability, defense, spacing and offensive chemistry.

Still, when this much talent gets stacked together, you just trust that it will figure things out. Edgecombe, a 21-year-old spring-loaded athlete with endless energy and on-court electricity, is the least notable member of this quintet and it's not close. That's how much firepower Philadelphia possesses.

James and Embiid have five MVPs between them. Brown and Maxey were All-NBA honorees last season. All four have averaged at least 28 points and five assists at least once within the past four seasons.

It could take time for everyone to find their footing, but if the pieces get aligned, this will be the best show in basketball and the best starting lineup in the league.

articles.title: Players and media hate Fever fans for one simple reason: They think they're conservative
articles.summary: Indiana Fever fans face repeated accusations of racism and right-wing politics, but investigations into incidents have yielded no supporting evidence.
articles.body: They don't hate them because they're White. A myriad of White fans have supported the WNBA since the league's inception, and they've backed Black players like Maya Moore, Lisa Leslie and Sheryl Swoopes with the same enthusiasm as they have White players like Sue Bird, Diana Taurasi, and Lauren Jackson. They don't hate them because they're "new," either. Players and media all want to see the league grow because it puts more money in their pockets or eyeballs on their stories. DETAILS EMERGE IN INCIDENT BETWEEN ACES STAR A'JA WILSON AND FEVER FAN DURING PLAYOFF GAME No, the reason there is such contempt for Indiana Fever fans — who seem to endure a new slight or attack every week — is for one reason: They're viewed as conservative. Former ESPN anchor Cari Champion put it about as plainly as possible in a podcast a couple weeks back when she said Fever star Caitlin Clark is "an avatar for middle America" and represents a fan base that "wants to spread hate." Translation: People who live in live flyover states are likely to be as backward as they are bigoted. A couple months earlier, CNN contributor Leah Asmelash wrote a column entitled: "How the right wing decided to care about women's basketball in Indiana," in which she zeroed in on conservatives' support for Clark and fellow Fever guard Sophie Cunningham. Before that, the Guardian's Manny Fidel published a piece entitled "The right's fury over Caitlin Clark is about everything except Caitlin Clark," with Fidel noting how "politicians, pundits and fans from across the right decried the decision" of Clark being left off the Olympic team. How he knew that the fans upset with the snub were on the right is unclear. That has simply become the assumption. First off, there is no way to know whether the majority of Fever fans are conservative or not. It's likely that most of them have simply been lured in by the two most popular players in the WNBA. One is Clark, who built an unprecedented fan base during her time at Iowa, where she was half Magic Johnson and half Steph Curry — pulling up from 28 feet several times per game while leading the nation in scoring and assists three times. The other is Cunningham, who, in addition to having end-your-marriage looks, is as effervescent and engaging as anyone in the sport. Her devoted following preceded any political stances she took. Nevertheless, these players' fans have been labeled "right wing," and that has predictable consequences in a league that overwhelmingly leans the other way. DAN DAKICH BLASTS A'JA WILSON OVER FAN INCIDENT IN PLAYOFF LOSS TO THE FEVER The most recent example, of course, is Aces forward A'ja Wilson furiously charging toward a Fever fan in the fourth quarter of Tuesday's playoff game in Indiana after he (gasp!) pointed at her and said "that (foul) is on you. As OutKick's Dan Zaksheske pointed out, none of the announcers or pundits on the Amazon Prime broadcast came to the fan's defense, and it was Wilson who later said that she was disrespected. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE This seems to keep happening, evidence be damned. In August, Aces guard Jackie Young had two fans removed from their seats at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis for "chirping all game," but an investigation determined that the fans hadn't violated any code of conduct. Last year, then-Chicago Sky forward Angel Reese claimed Fever fans hurled racist comments her way, but again, an investigation yielded no proof. And in 2024, then-Mercury center Brittney Griner said "I don't appreciate the new fans that sit there and yell racial slurs at myself, my teammates and the people they play against." We know what "new" fans she was talking about, but there wasn't a morsel of evidence backing up her words. PRIME VIDEO WNBA BROADCAST CREW EMBARRASSES ITSELF WITH COVERAGE OF A'JA WILSON FAN INCIDENT Unsurprisingly, no player, coach or mainstream media member has challenged any of these narratives. Why? Because they desperately want these so-called right-wing fans to be the villains. And when the evidence doesn't cooperate, it threatens their worldview and causes considerable consternation. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! It's sort of like when the Mueller report failed to establish criminal collusion between the Trump campaign and Russia. How many anti-Trumpers saw that and went "phew! The president isn't conspiring with a hostile foreign power!"? Approximately zero. Because they were seeking affirmation, not information. The WNBA is a league in which coaches, such as Cheryl Reeve, say that those who want to separate biological males and females in sports "don't want transgender people to exist." It's an organization in which players such as Wilson and DiJonai Carrington decry "white privilege." And a good chunk of the media who cover them walk in lockstep with their ideology. In their minds, fans ignoring such politics aren't everyday people who just want to watch hoops. They're deplorables. Perhaps the most egregious tweet regarding this matter came from USA Today writer Prince J. Grimes, who introduced his column Tuesday by writing "You can say A'ja Wilson overreacted, but in a split second of looking up, she perceived a fan's forward movement as a threat. In the context of everything with that fanbase, I can't blame her." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP No doubt there's a great deal of hate surrounding Fever fans. But it's not coming from them —it's coming toward them.

articles.title: Angel Reese Taunts Mystics in Viral Video with Allisha Gray After Dream's Win in WNBA Playoffs
articles.summary: DeWanna Bonner apparently wasn't happy to see Angel Reese and Allisha Gray taunting the Washington Mystics after sweeping them from the 2026 WNBA playoffs.
articles.body:
DeWanna Bonner apparently wasn't happy to see Angel Reese and Allisha Gray taunting the Washington Mystics after sweeping them from the 2026 WNBA playoffs.

The broadcast showed Reese and Gray waving and calling goodbye to the Mystics after a Wednesday night elimination victory before Bonner reached out to both and pushed their hands down to their sides.

Reese and Gray were reacting to a chippy 93-75 Game 2 win in which the two teams combined for 53 fouls.

The Dream had already come back from a double-digit Game 1 deficit to start out the series with a win. Atlanta will now advance to the semifinals after sweeping the best-of-three series.

The Dream will now advance to face the New York Liberty, which just became the first No. 8 seed in WNBA history to eliminate a No. 1 seed.

These two teams will begin a best-of-five battle for a spot in the WNBA title series Sunday in Atlanta.

articles.title: Los Cavaliers están en Málaga "como en casa"
articles.standfirst: El equipo de Cleveland comienza su concentración en The Embassy
articles.summary: El equipo de Cleveland comienza su concentración en The Embassy
articles.body: Málaga se ha convertido durante estos días en una de las paradas de referencia para los Cleveland Cavaliers. La franquicia de la NBA ya está instalada en la Costa del Sol, donde ha establecido su cuartel general de pretemporada en The Embassy, en Fuengirola. El conjunto de Kenny Atkinson cuenta entre sus filas con nombres de primer nivel como James Harden, Donovan Mitchell o Mario Hezonja, y permanecerá en tierras malagueñas hasta el domingo. La expedición de los Cavs llegó el martes y tuvo esa primera jornada para descansar, adaptarse al entorno y comenzar a combatir los efectos del cambio horario. Este miércoles llegó el momento de ponerse manos a la obra con el primer entrenamiento. La planificación contempla sesiones en The Embassy también durante jueves, viernes y sábado. El punto culminante llegará el domingo por la mañana. Cleveland se trasladará al Martín Carpena para realizar un entrenamiento a puerta abierta que apunta a congregar a una gran cantidad de aficionados. Será un fin de semana especialmente intenso para el Palacio, que el sábado ya habrá acogido el estreno del Unicaja como local en la Liga Endesa. El equipo cajista recibirá a La Laguna Tenerife a partir de las 19:30 horas. La presencia de los Cavaliers vuelve a poner el foco en la creciente relación entre Málaga y la NBA. La provincia se ha convertido en un destino cada vez más utilizado por jugadores y equipos de primer nivel para preparar sus temporadas. A ello se suma el protagonismo que ha adquirido The Embassy, el centro impulsado por Berni Rodríguez y José Manuel Calderón, y la posibilidad de que Unicaja participe en un futuro proyecto de la NBA en Europa. La estancia de Cleveland también ha permitido escuchar a algunas de las grandes figuras de su plantilla. James Harden fue uno de los protagonistas ante los medios y no escatimó elogios hacia su destino de pretemporada. "Málaga es increíble", aseguró la estrella estadounidense, satisfecha con las condiciones que está encontrando el equipo para trabajar. También habló Mario Hezonja, que encara con ilusión su nueva etapa en la NBA. El croata, además, dejó claro que espera con ganas el clima de Cleveland porque, según explicó, "odia el sol" y prefiere las bajas temperaturas de la ciudad estadounidense. El exjugador del Real Madrid también tuvo que responder por su salida del conjunto blanco. Hezonja explicó que estuvo "muy cerca" de continuar en Madrid pese al cambio en el banquillo, con la salida de Sergio Scariolo y la llegada de Pedro Martínez. Donovan Mitchell, por último, resumió sus sensaciones durante estos primeros días en la Costa del Sol con una frase sencilla: los Cavaliers se sienten en Málaga «como en casa».
